answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with vesting work credits. Each new identity starts at zero and earns credit only when a counterparty confirms a completed service; credits vest slowly, like a glacier advancing, so a fresh identity cannot transact until it builds a real work history. Credits are non-transferable, so one operator cannot pool them across fake identities. Verified counterparties form an oasis of trust, while unproven identities sit on the flat mesa of zero reputation. Forging a thousand Sybils means performing a thousand verified jobs, which costs more than the attack gains.
